label: Edge open unless a bridge or a ground-failure component on it closes it

inputs.name: damage
inputs.description: The damage state of every bridge whose `edge` is this edge, on the damage scale the closure policy is written for: zero, one or several parents.

inputs.name: liquefaction
inputs.description: The road state at every liquefaction component on this edge.

inputs.name: landslide
inputs.description: The road state at every landslide component on this edge.

inputs.name: fault
inputs.description: The road state at every fault crossing on this edge.

damage_scale.description: The damage-state quantity the closure policy reads.

usable_states.description: The damage states in which a bridge stays open to traffic.

description: Each bridge and each ground-failure component sits on one edge. The edge is open only if every bridge on it is in a damage state its closure policy keeps open and the road stays open at every ground-failure component on it, whatever its mechanism: they act in series. The CPT is a composite-state table (Byun & Song 2021): with the components in road order (chainage_km, read from the Bridge and GroundFailure tables; the binding's order where a component has none), row i says the first i-1 are open, the i-th is closed and the rest are in any state (edge closed), and the last row says every one is open (edge open): n + 1 disjoint rows for n components, instead of one row per combination of their states. Bind it to the edges that can close (where fixed_open is false); an edge that cannot is not a random variable.
